proofs.proof_tex:
Let \(\mu_a\) denote the marginal law of \((Y_t(a),D_t(a))\).  By ass:iid-arrivals, the current vector of potential outcome--delay pairs is independent of \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\) and has its common law.  By ass:sequential-randomization, conditional on \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\), on \(W_t=a\), and on the current potential vector, the assignment contributes the predictable factor \(\pi_t(a)\).  Consequently, after integrating out the unassigned component, the conditional kernel for the newly consumed observed pair \(Z_t=(Y_t(W_t),D_t(W_t))\) is
\[
 P\{W_t=a,Z_t\in dz\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}\}
 =\pi_t(a)\mu_a(dz).
\]
The revelation at \(t+D_t(W_t)\) is a deterministic measurable operation on \(t,W_t,Z_t\).  Thus, if \(h_{t-1}\) is any possible delayed observed history, the transition kernel from \(h_{t-1}\) first draws \(a\) with probabilities \(\pi_t(a;h_{t-1})\), then draws \(z\) from \(\mu_a\), and schedules the corresponding revelation.

Now put on an auxiliary space independent sequences \(\{Z_{a,j}:j\geq1\}\), \(a\in\{0,1\}\), with \(Z_{a,j}\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}\mu_a\), the two sequences being independent.  At assignment \(W_t=a\), consume \(Z_{a,N_a(t)}\).  Conditional on the delayed history and \(W_t=a\), that unused tape entry has law \(\mu_a\) and is independent of the history.  Hence this construction has exactly the transition kernel displayed above.  Induction on \(t=1,\ldots,T\) proves equality of all finite-dimensional laws of assignments, logged propensities, scheduled revelation times, and records revealed by every calendar time \(s\leq H_T\).  In particular it proves equality of the law of \(O_{T,\Delta}\).  Dependence between \((Y_t(0),D_t(0))\) and \((Y_t(1),D_t(1))\) causes no discrepancy: only one of those two components enters the displayed observed kernel.

Every deterministic prefix \((Z_{a,1},\ldots,Z_{a,K})\) is therefore an iid \(\mu_a\)-sample, and the two represented prefixes are independent.  This is an unconditional assertion; no event involving the calendar times at which the entries are consumed has been conditioned upon.

For the requested smallest adaptive stress test, take \(T=2\) and any finite-support \(\mu_0,\mu_1\).  Let the second assignment probability be one value when the first response has been revealed with positive sign, another when it has been revealed with nonpositive sign, and a third when it is still pending.  For \(a_1,a_2\in\mathcal A\) and tape values \(z_1,z_2\), both the arrival model and the tape model assign the cylinder the probability
\[
 \pi_1(a_1)\mu_{a_1}(z_1)
 \pi_2(a_2;h_1(a_1,z_1))\mu_{a_2}(z_2).
\]
The history \(h_1\) uses \(z_1\) only when its delay makes it observable.  The equality holds for every atom and uses no factorization of the outcome and delay within \(z_1\).  This verifies exactly that reward-dependent switching and informative delay do not invalidate the reduction.

Write \(I_t(a)=\mathbf 1\{W_t=a\}\).  Predictability permits the usual inverse-transform realization with independent \(U_t\sim\operatorname{Unif}(0,1)\): \(I_t(1)=\mathbf 1\{U_t\leq\pi_t(1)\}\).  For arm \(1\), set \(Z_t(1)=\mathbf 1\{U_t\leq ct^{-\alpha}\}\).  Under either design class, the relevant lower-envelope assumption gives \(Z_t(1)\leq I_t(1)\) almost surely, while the \(Z_t(1)\) are independent Bernoulli variables with means \(e_1(t)\).  For arm \(0\), set \(Z_t(0)=\mathbf 1\{U_t>1-\varepsilon\}\).  Ass:control-floor gives this domination on \(\mathfrak M_T^{\mathrm{low}}\); on \(\mathfrak M_T\), ass:rare-arm-envelope and \(C\leq1-\varepsilon\) give
\[
 \pi_t(0)=1-\pi_t(1)\geq1-Ct^{-\alpha}\geq\varepsilon.
\]
Thus \(Z_t(0)\leq I_t(0)\) in both classes, and \(Z_t(0)\) are independent Bernoulli variables with means \(e_0(t)=\varepsilon\).

Fix \(a\) and \(s\), put \(S_a(s)=\sum_{t\leq s}Z_t(a)\), \(Q=Q_a(s)\), and \(x=\sqrt{8Q\log T}\).  For \(0<x<Q\), exponential Markov and independence give, for every \(\lambda>0\),
\[
 P\{S_a(s)\leq Q-x\}
 \leq \exp\{\lambda(Q-x)+Q(e^{-\lambda}-1)\}.
\]
Taking \(\lambda=-\log(1-x/Q)\), and using
\[
 (1-u)\log(1-u)+u\geq u^2/2,\qquad 0\leq u<1,
\]
whose derivative comparison follows from \(-\log(1-u)\geq u\), yields
\[
 P\{S_a(s)\leq Q-x\}\leq \exp\{-x^2/(2Q)\}=T^{-4}.
\]
Because \(N_a(s)\geq S_a(s)\), the same bound applies to \(N_a(s)\).  At \(s=n_T\) and \(s=k_T\), \(Q_a(s)/\log T\to\infty\), so for all sufficiently large \(T\) the maximum with \(2\) in \(K_a(s)\) is inactive and \(K_a(s)\leq Q_a(s)-x\).  A union bound over the two arms and two deadlines proves
\[
 P(E_T^c)\leq4T^{-4}.
\]

Finally, integral comparison gives
\[
 \sum_{t\leq s}t^{-\alpha}
 =\frac{s^{1-\alpha}}{1-\alpha}\{1+o(1)\}.
\]
Since \(n_T=T-\lfloor T^\rho\rfloor\sim T\), \(k_T=\lfloor T^\rho\rfloor\), and \(\sqrt{Q_a(s)\log T}=o(Q_a(s))\), the quota definition implies
\[
 K_1(n_T)\asymp T^{1-\alpha},\quad
 K_0(n_T)\asymp T,\quad
 J_1=K_1(k_T)\asymp T^{\rho(1-\alpha)},\quad
 J_0=K_0(k_T)\asymp T^\rho.
\]
All constants depend only on the fixed envelope constants, so the probability and order assertions are uniform over both policy classes.

Work under the unconditional arm-tape representation of lem:arm-tape-equivalence.  Since \(m_T=k_T=\lfloor T^\rho\rfloor=o(T)\), for all sufficiently large \(T\),
\[
 0\leq g_{T,\Delta}<h_{T,\Delta},
 \qquad
 h_{T,\Delta}=T+\Delta_T-k_T.
\]
For each arm the tape entries are iid, so the definitions give
\[
 P M_{a,\Delta}=P\!\left[Y(a)\mathbf 1\{D(a)\leq g_{T,\Delta}\}\right],
 \quad
 P U_{a,\Delta}=P\!\left[Y(a)\mathbf 1\{g_{T,\Delta}<D(a)\leq h_{T,\Delta}\}\right].
\]
The two indicator sets are disjoint and their union is \(\{D(a)\leq h_{T,\Delta}\}\); hence
\[
 P(M_{a,\Delta}+U_{a,\Delta})
 =P\!\left[Y(a)\mathbf 1\{D(a)\leq h_{T,\Delta}\}\right].
\]
Subtracting the two arms and comparing with the definition of \(\tau\) shows
\[
 P\widehat\tau_{T,\Delta}=\tau-b_{T,\Delta}.
\]

By ass:bounded-outcomes and ass:polynomial-delay-envelope,
\[
 \left|P\!\left[Y(a)\mathbf 1\{D(a)>h_{T,\Delta}\}\right]\right|
 \leq P\{D(a)>h_{T,\Delta}\}
 \leq \min\{1,L(1+h_{T,\Delta})^{-\beta}\}.
\]
The triangle inequality gives \(|b_{T,\Delta}|\leq B_{T,\Delta}\).  Moreover,
\[
 \frac{1+h_{T,\Delta}}{1+T+\Delta_T}
 =1-\frac{k_T}{1+T+\Delta_T}=1+o(1)
\]
uniformly over deterministic \(\Delta_T\geq0\).  Since \(h_{T,\Delta}\to\infty\), the minimum in \(B_{T,\Delta}\) is eventually inactive, and therefore
\[
 B_{T,\Delta}=2L(1+T+\Delta_T)^{-\beta}\{1+o(1)\}.
\]

For \(R=Y(a)\mathbf 1\{g_{T,\Delta}<D(a)\leq h_{T,\Delta}\}\), the same two assumptions imply
\[
 P R^2\leq P\{D(a)>g_{T,\Delta}\}\leq
 v_{T,\Delta}.
\]
Thus \(\operatorname{Var}(U_{a,\Delta})\leq v_{T,\Delta}/J_a\).  The two arm tapes are independent, so
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(U_{1,\Delta}-U_{0,\Delta})
 \leq v_{T,\Delta}(J_1^{-1}+J_0^{-1}).
\]
Because \(g_{T,\Delta}\geq m_T\), the tail envelope gives
\[
 v_{T,\Delta}=O(T^{-\rho\beta}).
\]
The quota formula itself, by the integral comparison used in the proof of lem:quota-success, gives \(J_1\asymp T^{\rho(1-\alpha)}\) and \(J_0\asymp T^\rho\).  Consequently,
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(U_{1,\Delta}-U_{0,\Delta})
 =O\!\left(T^{-\rho\{\beta+1-\alpha\}}\right).
\]
The defining inequality
\(\rho>(1-\alpha)/(1-\alpha+\beta)\) is exactly
\(\rho(\beta+1-\alpha)>1-\alpha\).  Hence the last display is
\(o(T^{-(1-\alpha)})\), uniformly over both classes and all deterministic nonnegative follow-up sequences.

Put \(K_a=K_a(n_T)\), \(J_a=K_a(k_T)\), \(\sigma_a^2=\operatorname{Var}_P(X_{a,1}^{\Delta})\), and
\[
 Z_T=(M_{1,\Delta}-PM_{1,\Delta})-(M_{0,\Delta}-PM_{0,\Delta}),
 \qquad
 C_T=(U_{1,\Delta}-PU_{1,\Delta})-(U_{0,\Delta}-PU_{0,\Delta}).
\]
On \(E_T\), lem:old-cohort-correction gives the exact decomposition
\[
 \widehat\tau_{T,\Delta}-\tau+b_{T,\Delta}=Z_T+C_T. \tag{1}
\]

\emph{Measurability.}
On \(E_T\), the first \(K_a\) assignments to arm \(a\) occur by \(n_T\), hence have age at least \(H_T-n_T=g_{T,\Delta}\) at the terminal time.  The first \(J_a\) occur by \(k_T\), hence have age at least \(H_T-k_T=h_{T,\Delta}\).  A record revealed by those ages supplies its outcome and delay; absence of a revelation by the corresponding age makes the relevant truncated indicator zero.  Thus every \(X_{a,j}^{\Delta}\), \(R_{a,j}^{\Delta}\), sample variance, gate, and interval endpoint is a measurable function of \(O_{T,\Delta}\).  The conventions on \(E_T^c\) are measurable as well.

\emph{The concentration branch.}
For independent centered variables in an interval of length \(2\), convexity of the exponential gives
\[
 P\{|Z_T|\geq\sqrt{2S_Tx}\}\leq2e^{-x},
 \qquad S_T=K_1^{-1}+K_0^{-1}. \tag{2}
\]
For completeness, this follows by applying
\(P\exp\{\lambda(X-PX)\}\leq\exp(\lambda^2/2)\)
to each weighted tape variable and optimizing over \(\lambda\).
For a centered \(R\), \(|R-PR|\leq2\) and
\(P(R-PR)^2\leq PR^2\leq v_{T,\Delta}\).  Expanding its exponential series and using
\(|R-PR|^j\leq2^{j-2}(R-PR)^2\), \(j\geq2\), gives, after exponential Markov optimization,
\[
 P\!\left\{|U_{a,\Delta}-PU_{a,\Delta}|
 >\sqrt{\frac{2v_{T,\Delta}x}{J_a}}+\frac{4x}{3J_a}\right\}
 \leq2e^{-x}. \tag{3}
\]
With \(x=x_\eta=\log(6/\eta)\), (2), the two bounds (3), and a union bound have total failure probability at most \(\eta\).  On their joint complement, (1) and \(|b_{T,\Delta}|\leq B_{T,\Delta}\) imply
\(\tau\in I_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm{conc}}\).  Intersecting with \([-2,2]\) cannot remove \(\tau\).  Since the actual interval is \([-2,2]\) on \(E_T^c\), this argument is unconditional: the deviation event is defined on the complete tapes, and no conditioning on \(E_T\) occurs.

\emph{Uniform Gaussian approximation above the variance threshold.}
Define
\[
 V_T=\sigma_1^2+\mathbf 1\{\alpha=0\}\sigma_0^2.
\]
Consider first the triangular-array regime \(V_T\geq1/\log T\).  If \(\alpha>0\), then
\[
 s_{T,\Delta}^2\geq\frac{1}{K_1\log T};
\]
if \(\alpha=0\), comparability of \(K_0\) and \(K_1\) gives
\[
 s_{T,\Delta}^2\geq \frac{c_0}{T\log T}
\]
for a fixed \(c_0>0\).  The largest absolute summand of \(Z_T/s_{T,\Delta}\) is consequently
\[
 O\!\left(\sqrt{\frac{\log T}{K_1}}\right)=o(1)
\]
for \(\alpha>0\), and \(O(\sqrt{\log T/T})=o(1)\) for \(\alpha=0\).  The normalized summands are independent, centered, bounded, and their variances sum to one.

Here is a direct triangular-array argument.  If \(\xi_{Tj}\) are those normalized summands and
\(\delta_T=\max_j|\xi_{Tj}|\), Taylor's formula gives, for each fixed \(t\),
\[
 \prod_jP e^{it\xi_{Tj}}
 =\exp\!\left\{-\frac{t^2}{2}
 +O\!\left(|t|^3\delta_T\sum_jP\xi_{Tj}^2
 +t^4\sum_j(P\xi_{Tj}^2)^2\right)\right\}
 \longrightarrow e^{-t^2/2}. \tag{4}
\]
Indeed \(\sum_j(P\xi_{Tj}^2)^2\leq\delta_T^2\).
Tightness follows from the unit variance.  Every weakly convergent subsequence has, by (4), Gaussian characteristic function, which uniquely determines \(N(0,1)\).  Thus \(Z_T/s_{T,\Delta}\Rightarrow N(0,1)\).  The bounds on \(\delta_T\) are uniform, so a contradiction-subsequence argument and continuity of \(\Phi\) strengthen this to
\[
 \sup_{P,\Pi}\sup_x
 \left|P\{Z_T/s_{T,\Delta}\leq x\}-\Phi(x)\right|\longrightarrow0 \tag{5}
\]
over the stated high-variance regime.

The correction is negligible there.  Lem:old-cohort-correction and the lower bound for \(s_{T,\Delta}^2\) yield
\[
 \frac{P C_T^2}{s_{T,\Delta}^2}
 \leq
 C(\log T)T^{1-\alpha-\rho(\beta+1-\alpha)}
 \longrightarrow0. \tag{6}
\]
For sample variances, with \(K\geq2\),
\[
 \widehat\sigma^2=\frac{K}{K-1}\{\overline{X^2}-\bar X^2\}.
\]
Since \(|X|\leq1\), Chebyshev applied to \(\overline{X^2}\) and \(\bar X\) gives
\[
 \widehat\sigma_a^2-\sigma_a^2=O_P(K_a^{-1/2}) \tag{7}
\]
uniformly.  When \(\alpha>0\), divide the arm-one term in (7) by
\(\sigma_1^2\geq1/\log T\); the arm-zero weighted error is bounded, relative to \(s_{T,\Delta}^2\), by
\[
 O_P\!\left(\frac{K_1\log T}{K_0^{3/2}}\right)=o_P(1).
\]
When \(\alpha=0\), the two \(K_a\)'s are comparable to \(T\), and division by
\(\sigma_1^2+\sigma_0^2\geq1/\log T\) gives the same conclusion.  Hence
\[
 \widehat s_{T,\Delta}/s_{T,\Delta}\longrightarrow1 \tag{8}
\]
uniformly in the high-variance regime.  Equations (1), (5), (6), and (8), together with \(P(E_T^c)\to0\), prove the asserted studentized approximation there, with any measurable extension of the displayed quotient on \(E_T^c\).

On the regular class, truncation does not destroy the variance floor.  Indeed, if
\(X=Y\mathbf 1\{D\leq g_{T,\Delta}\}\), then
\[
 |\operatorname{Var}(X)-\operatorname{Var}(Y)|
 \leq |P(X^2-Y^2)|+|(PX)^2-(PY)^2|
 \leq3P\{D>g_{T,\Delta}\}\leq3v_{T,\Delta}. \tag{9}
\]
Thus ass:regular-variance and \(v_{T,\Delta}\to0\) imply \(V_T\geq\kappa/2\) eventually (with an immaterial adjustment of the constant when \(\alpha=0\)).  This places the whole regular class in the regime of (5)--(8) and proves both uniform assertions in the theorem, without any convergence requirement on \(t^\alpha\pi_t(1)\).

\emph{The gate and bounded-shift coverage.}
For \(B\geq0\) define \(f_B(s)=s\,c_\eta(B/s)\), \(s>0\).  If \(Z\sim N(0,1)\), then
\[
 P\{|sZ-b|\leq f_B(s)\}
 =\Phi(c_\eta(B/s)+b/s)+\Phi(c_\eta(B/s)-b/s)-1
 \geq1-\eta \tag{10}
\]
for every \(|b|\leq B\), because the last expression decreases with \(|b|\) and the defining equation for \(c_\eta\) is equality at \(|b|=B\).
Let \(z_\gamma=\Phi^{-1}(\gamma)\).  The defining equation also gives
\[
 B+z_{1-\eta}s\leq f_B(s)\leq B+z_{1-\eta/2}s. \tag{11}
\]
Moreover \(f_B\) is uniformly Lipschitz in \(s\), with a constant depending only on \(\eta\).  To see this, write \(u=B/s\), \(x=c_\eta(u)-u\).  Then
\[
 z_{1-\eta}\leq x\leq z_{1-\eta/2},\qquad
 0\leq c_\eta'(u)
 =\frac{\phi(c_\eta(u)-u)-\phi(c_\eta(u)+u)}
 {\phi(c_\eta(u)-u)+\phi(c_\eta(u)+u)}
 \leq1.
\]
Hence
\[
 f_B'(s)=x+\frac{2u\phi(x+2u)}{\phi(x)+\phi(x+2u)}
\]
is bounded uniformly over \(B,u,s\).  Therefore (5)--(8), (10), and a deterministic-endpoint sandwich imply that \(I_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm G}\) has coverage at least \(1-\eta-o(1)\) throughout \(V_T\geq1/\log T\).  The extra radius \(d_{T,\Delta}\) can only increase coverage; from the quota orders and the choice of \(\rho\),
\[
 d_{T,\Delta}
 =O\!\left(
 \sqrt{T^{-\rho(\beta+1-\alpha)}\log T}
 +T^{-\rho(1-\alpha)}\log T\right)
 =o(T^{-q}). \tag{12}
\]
This includes arrays with \(V_T\) of order \(1/\log T\).

It remains to verify that data-dependent splicing does not spend the error probability twice.  If \(V_T\leq1/\log T\), (7) and Chebyshev imply
\[
 \sup_{P,\Pi}P(G_{T,\Delta})\longrightarrow0, \tag{13}
\]
because the gate is separated from \(V_T\) by \(1/\log T\) and
\((\log T)^2/K_1\to0\).  The concentration branch then gives coverage
\(1-\eta-o(1)\).
If \(V_T>1/\log T\), use Gaussian coverage.  On \(G_{T,\Delta}^c\), the bounded empirical variance and the gate imply
\[
 \widehat s_{T,\Delta}=o(T^{-q})
\]
deterministically: for \(\alpha>0\),
\(\widehat s^2\leq2/(K_1\log T)+2/K_0\), and for \(\alpha=0\),
\(\widehat s^2=O(1/(T\log T))\).
By (11), (12), and
\(a_T=\sqrt{2S_Tx_\eta}\asymp T^{-q}\),
\[
 f_{B_{T,\Delta}}(\widehat s_{T,\Delta})+d_{T,\Delta}
 \leq B_{T,\Delta}+o(a_T)
 \leq B_{T,\Delta}+a_T+A_{1,T,\Delta}(x_\eta)+A_{0,T,\Delta}(x_\eta)
\]
for all sufficiently large \(T\).  Thus \(I_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm{conc}}\) contains
\(I_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm G}\) on gate failure.  The selected interval consequently contains the Gaussian interval throughout the high-variance regime, while (13) makes its Gaussian selection negligible in the low-variance regime.  Combining the two cases, and recalling that quota failure returns the full parameter interval, proves uniform honesty over the union of model classes.  It also establishes exactly the claimed observable variance-gate and fallback behavior.

The coverage assertion is the uniform-honesty conclusion of thm:uniform-gated-inference.  We first prove the upper length bound.  The quota orders imply
\[
 S_T=O(T^{-(1-\alpha)}),\qquad
 a_T=O(T^{-q}).
\]
The calculation in lem:old-cohort-correction, with fixed \(x_\eta\), gives
\[
 A_{1,T,\Delta}(x_\eta)+A_{0,T,\Delta}(x_\eta)=o(T^{-q}),
\]
and (12) in the proof of thm:uniform-gated-inference gives
\(d_{T,\Delta}=o(T^{-q})\).  Since a sample variance of observations in
\([-1,1]\) is at most \(2\), \(\widehat s_{T,\Delta}=O(\sqrt{S_T})=O(T^{-q})\).
The upper inequality in (11) gives
\[
 \widehat s_{T,\Delta}
 c_\eta(B_{T,\Delta}/\widehat s_{T,\Delta})
 \leq B_{T,\Delta}+z_{1-\eta/2}\widehat s_{T,\Delta}.
\]
Also \(B_{T,\Delta}=O((1+H_T)^{-\beta})\), because
\((1+h_{T,\Delta})/(1+H_T)\to1\) uniformly over \(\Delta_T\geq0\).
Thus both branches have length \(O(r_{T,\Delta})\) on \(E_T\).  On \(E_T^c\)
the length is \(4\), and lem:quota-success gives a contribution at most
\(16T^{-4}=o(r_{T,\Delta})\).  This proves the stated uniform expected-length upper bound.

For the sampling lower bound, use one fixed deterministic admissible policy
\[
 \pi_t(1)=ct^{-\alpha},\qquad \pi_t(0)=1-ct^{-\alpha},
\]
and put all delays equal to zero.  Keep arm \(0\) identically zero.  In arm \(1\), under laws \(P_+\) and \(P_-\), let \(Y\in\{-1,1\}\) have means \(d_T\) and \(-d_T\), respectively.  Put
\[
 Q_T=\sum_{t\leq T}ct^{-\alpha},\qquad d_T=\lambda Q_T^{-1/2},
\]
where \(\lambda>0\) is fixed and small.  The one-observation Hellinger affinity between the two Rademacher laws is \(\sqrt{1-d_T^2}\); hence the affinity \(A_T\) between the complete logged experiments is
\[
 A_T=\prod_{t\leq T}
 \left[1-ct^{-\alpha}\{1-\sqrt{1-d_T^2}\}\right]
 \geq1-\sum_{t\leq T}ct^{-\alpha}d_T^2
 =1-\lambda^2. \tag{14}
\]
This calculation includes assignments and logged propensities, whose laws are common.  For any two dominated laws with affinity \(A\), Cauchy--Schwarz gives directly
\[
 \|P-Q\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 =\frac12\int|\sqrt p-\sqrt q|(\sqrt p+\sqrt q)
 \leq\sqrt{1-A^2}. \tag{15}
\]
Thus the total variation in (14) is at most \(\sqrt2\lambda\).  If an interval
\(J_{T,\Delta}\) covers both targets with probability at least \(1-\eta\), then under \(P_+\) it contains both target points with probability at least
\(1-2\eta-\sqrt2\lambda\).  Choosing
\(\lambda<(1-2\eta)/\sqrt2\), and noting that the targets differ by
\(2d_T\), gives
\[
 \sup_{(P,\Pi,T)\in\mathfrak M_T}
 E_{P,\Pi}|J_{T,\Delta}|
 \geq 2d_T(1-2\eta-\sqrt2\lambda)
 \geq c_{\eta,1}T^{-q}. \tag{16}
\]

For the hidden-tail lower bound, retain the same policy and, independently in each arm, put probability
\[
 \delta_T=\min\{1/4,L(1+H_T)^{-\beta}\}
\]
on delay \(H_T+1\), with the remaining mass at \((Y,D)=(0,0)\).  Under
\(P_+\), give the delayed atom outcome \(+1\) in arm \(1\) and \(-1\) in arm \(0\); under \(P_-\), reverse both signs.  For \(u\leq H_T\),
\[
 P\{D>u\}=\delta_T\leq L(1+H_T)^{-\beta}\leq L(1+u)^{-\beta},
\]
and for \(u\geq H_T+1\) the tail is zero, so the polynomial envelope holds and every delay is finite.  No delayed atom can be revealed by \(H_T\).  The two observed experiments, including missingness, adaptive history, assignments, and logged propensities, therefore have exactly the same law under the same policy.  Their targets are \(2\delta_T\) and \(-2\delta_T\).  Under their common observed law, simultaneous coverage has probability at least \(1-2\eta\), whence
\[
 \sup_{(P,\Pi,T)\in\mathfrak M_T}
 E_{P,\Pi}|J_{T,\Delta}|
 \geq4\delta_T(1-2\eta)
 \geq c_{\eta,2}(1+H_T)^{-\beta} \tag{17}
\]
eventually.  Taking the maximum of (16) and (17) proves the lower bound by a constant multiple of \(r_{T,\Delta}\).  At \(\Delta_T=0\), \(H_T=T\), which gives the displayed frontier.

The proof of lem:quota-success uses only ass:one-sided-forced-exploration for arm \(1\) and ass:control-floor for arm \(0\); therefore its deterministic quota guarantee holds uniformly on \(\mathfrak M_T^{\mathrm{low}}\).  Lem:arm-tape-equivalence and lem:old-cohort-correction also hold on that class.  The concentration, gate, and studentization arguments in thm:uniform-gated-inference use the policy only through those deterministic quotas.  They therefore give
\[
 \inf_{(P,\Pi,T)\in\mathfrak M_T^{\mathrm{low}}}
 P\{\tau\in I_{T,\Delta}\}\geq1-\eta-o(1).
\]
The branchwise length calculation in the proof of thm:minimax-length-frontier likewise uses only the quota orders and the delay envelope, and hence gives
\[
 \sup_{(P,\Pi,T)\in\mathfrak M_T^{\mathrm{low}}}
 E_{P,\Pi}|I_{T,\Delta}|\leq C_\eta r_{T,\Delta}.
\]
The lower allocation envelope alone does not bound the actual number of designated-arm assignments from above.  Thus it cannot yield the sampling-information obstruction used in the converse, which is why no matching sampling lower bound is concluded on this enlarged class.

First record the Gaussian calibration implied by def:bounded-shift-critical-value.  For fixed \(c>0\) and \(v\geq0\),
\[
 P\{|Z-v|\leq c\}=\Phi(c-v)+\Phi(c+v)-1,\qquad Z\sim N(0,1).
\]
Its derivative in \(v\) is
\(\phi(c+v)-\phi(c-v)\leq0\).  Hence, among all shifts with absolute value at most \(u\), the least coverage occurs at absolute shift \(u\).  The left side of the defining equation for \(c_\eta(u)\) is continuous and strictly increasing from \(0\) to \(1\) as \(c\) runs from \(0\) to infinity, proving existence and uniqueness and showing that \(c_\eta(u)\) gives coverage exactly \(1-\eta\) at the endpoint shift.

Now let \(\Delta_T=0\) and \(\beta=q\).  On
\(\mathfrak M_{T,0}^{\mathrm{reg}}(\kappa)\), (9) in the proof of
thm:uniform-gated-inference and ass:regular-variance imply
\[
 s_{T,0}\asymp T^{-q}
\]
uniformly.  Lem:old-cohort-correction gives \(B_{T,0}=O(T^{-q})\), so
\(B_{T,0}/s_{T,0}\) is uniformly bounded.  The uniform studentized approximation,
\(\widehat s_{T,0}/s_{T,0}\to1\), the Lipschitz calculation for
\(f_B(s)=s c_\eta(B/s)\), and \(|b_{T,0}|\leq B_{T,0}\) therefore imply
\[
 \inf_{(P,\Pi,T)\in\mathfrak M_{T,0}^{\mathrm{reg}}(\kappa)}
 P\{\tau\in I_{T,0}^{\mathrm G}\}\geq1-\eta-o(1).
\]
The nonnegative correction radius \(d_{T,0}=o(s_{T,0})\) does not alter the limiting calibration.

We next exhibit attainment.  Use the deterministic policy
\(\pi_t(1)=ct^{-\alpha}\), and put
\[
 \delta_T=L(1+T)^{-q}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(T\), when \(\delta_T<1/4\).  In each arm, with probability \(1-\delta_T\), take \(D=0\) and let \(Y\) be a symmetric Rademacher variable.  With probability \(\delta_T\), take \(D=T+1\); under the plus law assign this hidden atom outcome \(+1\) in arm \(1\) and \(-1\) in arm \(0\), and under the minus law reverse the signs.  This iid triangular family obeys the delay envelope: for \(u\leq T\), its tail is \(\delta_T\leq L(1+u)^{-q}\), and after \(T+1\) it is zero.  Outcomes are bounded, delays are finite, and the deterministic policy satisfies both sides of ass:rare-arm-envelope.  Eventual outcome variances tend to one.

Because \(g_{T,0}<h_{T,0}<T+1\), the correction variables are identically zero, while each \(X\) is a symmetric Rademacher variable with probability \(1-\delta_T\) and zero otherwise.  Under the plus law,
\[
 \tau=2\delta_T,\qquad b_{T,0}=2\delta_T,\qquad
 s_{T,0}^2=(1-\delta_T)(K_1^{-1}+K_0^{-1}). \tag{18}
\]
Also
\[
 \frac{b_{T,0}}{B_{T,0}}
 =\frac{L(1+T)^{-q}}{L(1+h_{T,0})^{-q}}
 =\left(\frac{1+h_{T,0}}{1+T}\right)^q\longrightarrow1. \tag{19}
\]
The quota asymptotics give
\[
 \frac{B_{T,0}}{s_{T,0}}\longrightarrow
 u=
 \begin{cases}
 2L\sqrt{c/(1-\alpha)},&\alpha>0,\\[3pt]
 2L\bigl(c^{-1}+\varepsilon^{-1}\bigr)^{-1/2},&\alpha=0,
 \end{cases}
\]
which is finite and strictly positive.  The independent bounded triangular-array argument used in (4), together with \(P(E_T^c)\to0\), (18), and (19), yields
\[
 \frac{\widehat\tau_{T,0}-\tau}{s_{T,0}}
 =
 \frac{\widehat\tau_{T,0}-\tau+b_{T,0}}{s_{T,0}}
 -\frac{b_{T,0}}{s_{T,0}}
 \ \Rightarrow\ N(-u,1),
 \qquad
 \frac{B_{T,0}}{s_{T,0}}\to u.
\]
Sample-variance consistency also gives \(\widehat s_{T,0}/s_{T,0}\to1\).  Therefore, for every fixed \(c'>0\),
\[
 P\{\tau\in[\widehat\tau_{T,0}\pm c'\widehat s_{T,0}]\}
 \longrightarrow
 \Phi(c'-u)+\Phi(c'+u)-1.
\]
The first paragraph shows that choosing \(c'=c_\eta(u)\) makes this limit
\(1-\eta\), while every smaller symmetric critical value has smaller endpoint-shift coverage.  Thus the bounded-shift envelope is attained by a family in the actual delayed experiment.

On the regular class, (9) in the proof of thm:uniform-gated-inference and the deterministic quota orders imply
\[
 0<c_0T^{-2q}\leq s_{T,\Delta}^2\leq C_0T^{-2q}
\]
uniformly.  The studentized theorem and lem:old-cohort-correction give
\[
 \frac{\widehat\tau_{T,\Delta}-\tau}{\widehat s_{T,\Delta}}
 =
 \frac{\widehat\tau_{T,\Delta}-\tau+b_{T,\Delta}}
 {\widehat s_{T,\Delta}}
 -\frac{b_{T,\Delta}}{\widehat s_{T,\Delta}},
\qquad
 \sup\frac{|b_{T,\Delta}|}{s_{T,\Delta}}
 \leq C T^q(1+T+\Delta_T)^{-\beta}. \tag{20}
\]
If the last product tends to zero, the second term in (20) is uniformly
\(o_P(1)\), while the first is uniformly standard normal.  Hence the ordinary
\(z_{1-\eta/2}\) interval has uniform coverage \(1-\eta+o(1)\).

For necessity, use the deterministic policy and Rademacher-plus-hidden-atom construction from the proof of thm:attained-boundary-calibration, replacing the hidden delay \(T+1\) by \(H_T+1\) and taking
\[
 \delta_T=L(1+H_T)^{-\beta}
\]
eventually.  The hidden atoms remain unrevealed at \(H_T\), \(U_{a,\Delta}=0\), the visible variance still satisfies \(s_{T,\Delta}\asymp T^{-q}\), and
\[
 \frac{b_{T,\Delta}}{s_{T,\Delta}}
 \asymp T^q(1+H_T)^{-\beta}. \tag{21}
\]
If the product in (21) converges to a positive finite value, pass to its limit
\(u>0\).  The same triangular-array calculation gives a \(N(-u,1)\) limit, so ordinary-Wald coverage tends to
\[
 \Phi(z_{1-\eta/2}-u)+\Phi(z_{1-\eta/2}+u)-1<1-\eta.
\]
If the product diverges, the centered standardized statistic is tight whereas its deterministic shift diverges, and coverage tends to zero.  If the product merely fails to converge to zero, a subsequence has either a positive finite sublimit or diverges, and the corresponding construction refutes uniform asymptotic honesty along that subsequence.  This proves the if-and-only-if assertion.  At \(\Delta_T=0\), the product is \(T^{q-\beta}\{1+o(1)\}\), which tends to zero exactly when \(\beta>q\).

A stationary binary endpoint is a special case of ass:bounded-outcomes, and its risk difference is exactly the causal contrast \(\tau\).  Once the logged inferior-arm probabilities have been verified to satisfy ass:rare-arm-envelope and the endpoint ascertainment times satisfy ass:polynomial-delay-envelope, prop:wald-followup-frontier applies with terminal observation time \(H_T=T+\Delta_T\).  It proves that the unpadded interval \(I_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm W}\) is uniformly asymptotically honest over the entire informative-delay class exactly when
\[
 T^q(1+T+\Delta_T)^{-\beta}\longrightarrow0.
\]
When this condition is not certified, thm:uniform-gated-inference supplies the bias-aware Gaussian branch and concentration fallback, both computed from the same terminal records, or the protocol may increase its prespecified \(\Delta_T\) until the displayed product vanishes.  The necessity is class-wide: its witness varies the hidden outcome signs while leaving the observed experiment unchanged or asymptotically contiguous.  It therefore does not assert failure at a particular prompt-delay law, which proves the final qualification in the proposition.

Assume \(D_t(a)=0\) almost surely for both arms.  Since
\(g_{T,\Delta}\geq0\) and \(h_{T,\Delta}\geq0\) for all sufficiently large \(T\),
\[
 X_{a,j}^{\Delta}=Y_{a,j},\qquad
 R_{a,j}^{\Delta}=0,\qquad
 U_{a,\Delta}=0.
\]
Also \(\mathbf 1\{D(a)>h_{T,\Delta}\}=0\), so \(b_{T,\Delta}=0\).  Consequently
\[
 \widehat\tau_{T,\Delta}=M_{1,\Delta}-M_{0,\Delta}
\]
on quota success, a difference of two independent fixed-size tape means.  On the regular class, the bounded triangular-array argument and sample-variance calculation in thm:uniform-gated-inference therefore give pointwise standard-normal studentization, and \(I_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm W}\) is pointwise asymptotically honest.

The radius \(B_{T,\Delta}\) is defined from the whole polynomial envelope, not from the realized prompt-delay law, and \(L>0\); it therefore need not vanish.  The defining equation for \(c_\eta(u)\) is continuous and strictly increasing in its critical-value argument, so
\[
 c_\eta(u)\longrightarrow c_\eta(0)=z_{1-\eta/2}
 \quad\text{as }u\downarrow0.
\]
It follows that the generic Gaussian radius equals the ordinary-Wald radius to first order precisely along the stated sequences
\(B_{T,\Delta}/\widehat s_{T,\Delta}\to0\); the deterministic correction radius also satisfies \(d_{T,\Delta}/\widehat s_{T,\Delta}\to0\) on the regular prompt-delay law by (12).  Without the bias-ratio condition the generic procedure correctly retains its class-wide conservative tail pad.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The exact observed-experiment modulus and the optimal variable-length confidence procedure have not been characterized.
open_obligations.obstruction: The two-point sampling and hidden-tail experiments give matching orders but do not solve the joint Gaussian and partially identified variable-length interval optimization; the frozen constant handle does not itself define or prove the optimizer.
open_obligations.attempted: The proof derives the same-policy Hellinger sampling bound, the identical-law hidden-tail bound, and the attained symmetric bounded-shift Gaussian envelope. These certify the rate and one boundary face, but they do not establish convergence of the normalized global minimax value or characterize every optimal randomized interval.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The proved results determine the order
\[
 \max\{T^{-(1-\alpha)/2},T^{-\beta}\}
\]
at zero extra follow-up and identify the exact symmetric Gaussian critical value on an attained bounded-shift boundary family.  They do not determine the normalized minimax expected-length limit over all variable-length or randomized intervals.
